facebook.long_form:
🏀 Training camp doesn't open for weeks — but the Philadelphia 76ers are already competing at 6:15 in the morning.

Tyrese Maxey beat LeBron James to the gym earlier this week and made sure everyone knew about it. He posted a public callout. LeBron's response? He posted a workout photo captioned "Rese for President."

This is not just chemistry. This is culture.

LeBron (41 years old, the greatest statistical player in NBA history) and Maxey (one of the most dynamic young point guards in the league) share the same agent in Rich Paul, which means they've had years of familiarity before this season even started. But the dynamic in Philadelphia feels different. Maxey is the heartbeat of this franchise — and LeBron is making sure that message is loud and clear.

The projected starting five heading into camp: LeBron James, Joel Embiid, Jaylen Brown, Tyrese Maxey, and Jared Edgecombe. That group collectively holds FIVE NBA MVP awards. Embiid's health has been confirmed by the coaching staff. The preseason reportedly opens October 8 at Barclays Center in Brooklyn.

This team was built to win. And before training camp, before the preseason, before a single regular-season minute — they're already competing for each other.

💬 Is this the most talented team in the NBA right now? Or is the Knicks' championship core still the team to beat in the East?

stories.title: Wembanyama Back in France — FIBA Return and Spurs Camp
stories.angle: Victor Wembanyama named to France's FIBA World Cup qualifying roster, posts "I miss FIBA"; hosting several Spurs teammates in France for workouts

x_posts.label: Post 2
x_posts.text:
Victor Wembanyama: "I miss FIBA."

Named to France's 2027 World Cup qualifying roster. Hosting Spurs teammates in France for summer workouts.

Defending DPoY. WCF MVP. 2024 Olympic gold medalist.

The guy does everything. 🇫🇷

#Spurs #NBA

facebook.long_form:
🇫🇷 Victor Wembanyama is back in France — and he's already thinking about more than basketball.

Wembanyama has been named to France's 15-man roster for the 2027 FIBA World Cup qualifying window this August. When asked about the call-up, he was characteristically direct: "I miss FIBA."

It's been nearly two years since Wembanyama helped France win the gold medal at the 2024 Paris Olympics in front of his home crowd. In between, he won Defensive Player of the Year, earned All-NBA honors, and led San Antonio to the Western Conference Finals — where he won MVP. He closed his third NBA season as perhaps the most dominant two-way player on the planet.

And yet — he misses FIBA.

Wembanyama is hosting several Spurs teammates in France this offseason for informal workouts. ESPN confirmed the group includes De'Aaron Fox, Stephon Castle, and Dylan Harper. This is what team-building looks like away from the arena.

France is scheduled to play Serbia on August 20 and 23 before World Cup qualifying games against Slovenia (Aug 27) and Sweden (Aug 30). For Wembanyama, this isn't an obligation — it's a reunion.

Meanwhile, his Spurs future is secure: he signed a five-year, $252 million extension, deliberately choosing the 25% max salary tier rather than the 30% supermax — leaving approximately $50 million on the table to help San Antonio remain financially flexible.

At 22, he's the best player on the planet. And he still misses FIBA.

💬 Does Wembanyama win a championship with the Spurs before his contract is up? Drop your prediction below.

stories.title: LeBron's Historic Triple — 42K+ Points, 11K+ Rebounds, 11K+ Assists
stories.angle: LeBron closed 2025-26 as the only player in NBA history with 42,000+ points, 11,000+ rebounds, and 11,000+ assists simultaneously. The statistical case for the GOAT debate.

x_posts.label: Post 4
x_posts.text:
LeBron James closed 2025-26 with 43,440 career points.

He is the ONLY player in NBA history with:
— 42,000+ points
— 11,000+ rebounds
— 11,000+ assists

No one else has ever done all three.

And he just signed with the 76ers to chase more. 👑

#LeBron #NBA

facebook.long_form:
👑 The greatest statistical player in NBA history just joined your Philadelphia 76ers.

Here's what LeBron James closed the 2025-26 season with:

**Career totals:**
— 43,440 points (most all-time, first player ever past 42,000)
— 11,000+ rebounds
— 11,000+ assists

He is the only player in NBA history to achieve all three of those marks simultaneously. No one else. Not Jordan. Not Kareem. Not Magic. Not Shaq. Not Wilt.

Just LeBron.

To put the scoring in perspective: Kevin Durant passed Michael Jordan for No. 5 on the all-time list during the same 2025-26 season. Durant's career total? Roughly 30,000 points. LeBron has 13,000 more than that.

Stephen Curry passed Kevin Garnett, John Havlicek, and Paul Pierce on the scoring list last season, with Tim Duncan's 26,496 as his next target. LeBron crossed 26,496 points... several years ago.

And somehow, at age 41, he's walking into a new chapter in Philadelphia with something to prove.

The GOAT debate is over. The legacy-building continues.

💬 Has any player ever accomplished what LeBron has statistically? Sound off below.

stories.title: Fred VanVleet Opts Into $25M — Houston's Starting PG Returns From Torn ACL
stories.angle: Despite missing all of 2025-26 with a torn ACL, VanVleet opted into his $25M player option with Houston; recovery on track for training camp

x_posts.label: Post 5
x_posts.text:
Fred VanVleet tore his ACL in September 2025 and missed all of last season.

He just opted INTO his $25M player option with Houston anyway.

He's betting on his recovery. And the Rockets are betting on him.

Training camp can't come soon enough. 💪

#Rockets #NBA

facebook.long_form:
💪 Fred VanVleet tore his ACL in September of 2025. He missed the entire 2025-26 season — every game, every moment, every playoff run.

And when the opt-in deadline came, he opted into his $25M player option with the Houston Rockets anyway.

He's betting everything on his recovery.

VanVleet, 32, has been one of the more underrated point guards of his generation — a player who went undrafted, won a championship with Toronto, and rebuilt himself as a legitimate starter in Houston. When the ACL gave out, many wondered if the comeback would be complete enough to justify the cost.

His answer was $25 million worth of confidence.

The Rockets are betting on him too. If VanVleet returns at or near his previous level, he gives Houston a proven, championship-tested floor general to pair with their emerging young core. If the recovery falls short, they're carrying a significant salary for production they may not get.

Training camp opens in late September. That's when we'll see where Fred VanVleet's body actually is.

But for now, count him in.

💬 Can VanVleet return fully from a torn ACL at 32? Or is this a risk Houston will regret?

---
